fields.statement: At 04deb2ed I built rhiza with go build -o $TMPDIR/rhiza-qa ./cmd/rhiza and used it in a scratch git repo: landed A adding capabilities base and other, proposed B setting base.statement, drafts C (base.statement, other.acceptance) and D (other.acceptance, current). rhiza overlaps printed 'No overlaps' and --json {"overlaps": []} with D current, so the current draft is not counted unless named. --change C printed 'change sets B and C both write field:statement of base' and JSON with a, b, target base and aspects [field:statement]; rhiza api call overlaps --change C gave byte-identical output. --change D gave No overlaps (unnamed draft C ignored), --change B (proposed) gave No overlaps, a 10-char prefix and RHIZA_CHANGE both resolved C, an unknown ID exited 4 with 'no change set'. After proposing C, --change D listed B/C on base and C/D on field:acceptance of other. go test of internal/model Overlap and the overlaps and describe-golden scripts pass.

At 04deb2ed the built binary's rhiza guide plan-review prints, at line 24, the paragraph telling the reviewer to run `rhiza overlaps --change <cs> --json` for each plan change set and record each contradicting overlap as a `contradiction` finding naming the other change set. I ran that command as the guide says against a scratch repo and it returned the overlap JSON the guide describes. go test ./internal/guide -count=1 passes (TestPlanReviewText and the cap tests).
